interactions.effectSize: HOMA-IR −0.14 (−0.51 to 0.23) at 6 months, very low certainty (T2D); keto HOMA SMD −0.29 in diabetic subgroup
interactions.population: adults with T2D; adults with obesity
interactions.mechanism: Less carbohydrate means less insulin secretion; liver fat falls

interactions.effectSize: HOMA-IR −2.4 % (−4.6 to −0.3) per 5 %E carbohydrate → MUFA
interactions.mechanism: Lower insulin demand; MUFA improves sensitivity
Weight-loss and satiety effects; amino acids also stimulate insulin acutely

interactions.effectSize: Fasting insulin −2.00 µU/mL (−3.02 to −0.97); HOMA-IR −0.58 (−0.81 to −0.35)
interactions.population: non-diabetic adults, TRE without calorie restriction
interactions.mechanism: Longer daily low-insulin window; small weight loss

interactions.effectSize: Long-term: fasting insulin −0.89 µU/mL (−1.56 to −0.22) vs continuous restriction. Acute: after a 24 h fast insulin sensitivity index 5.7 → 2.6 (×10⁻⁴ min⁻¹ per mU/L)
interactions.mechanism: Low insulin during the fast; high free fatty acids cause transient insulin resistance afterwards

interactions.effectSize: Insulin falls during the fast; peripheral insulin resistance develops (see 60 h data). A fasting insulin drawn in the 1–3 days after is not a baseline
interactions.mechanism: Glucose sparing via fatty-acid oxidation

interactions.effectSize: Insulin-mediated glucose uptake −46 % after 60 h
interactions.mechanism: Glucose sparing; ~ninefold free fatty acids

interactions.effectSize: Fasting insulin −1.1 pmol/L (−1.7 to −0.5) per 5 %E carbohydrate → SFA (≈ −0.2 µU/mL, negligible); worse than PUFA
interactions.mechanism: SFA impairs insulin sensitivity relative to PUFA

interactions.effectSize: One small study: HOMA-IR lower with eggs
interactions.mechanism: Displacement of refined carbohydrate

interactions.effectSize: HOMA-IR −1.24 (−1.72 to −0.76); insulin SMD −2.03
interactions.mechanism: Lower post-meal insulin demand; SCFA effects

interactions.effectSize: Fasting insulin −1.6 pmol/L (−2.8 to −0.4) per 5 %E carbohydrate → PUFA
interactions.mechanism: Better insulin sensitivity

interactions.effectSize: Fasting insulin SMD −0.19 (−0.35 to −0.02); in women −0.23, none in men
interactions.mechanism: Unclear; not a lever to recommend

interactions.effectSize: Acute insulin sensitivity SMD −2.06; a coffee before the blood draw can raise fasting insulin
interactions.mechanism: Adrenaline release and adenosine block

interactions.effectSize: No data opened
interactions.mechanism: Mechanistic expectation only (muscle GLUT4)

interactions.mechanism: Satiety and weight effects; fasting state

interactions.effectSize: No fasting-insulin data opened; HbA1c falls in T2D
interactions.mechanism: More muscle mass for glucose disposal

interactions.effectSize: HOMA-IR unchanged after 4 weeks of training without weight change (engine research)
interactions.mechanism: Benefit is in muscle insulin sensitivity, which fasting insulin captures poorly

interactions.effectSize: Insulin sensitivity −20 % after one short night
interactions.mechanism: Hepatic and peripheral insulin resistance

Insulin-signalling cofactor

interactions.effectSize: Fasting insulin −1.16 µU/mL (−1.91 to −0.40), high-quality studies only
interactions.mechanism: Catechins

interactions.effectSize: Fasting insulin and HOMA-IR improved (magnitude not in abstract)
interactions.mechanism: Unclear

interactions.effectSize: No significant insulin change in obesity/prediabetes
interactions.mechanism: Ketones do not raise insulin load

interactions.effectSize: Pooled ketogenic RCTs +0.26 mg/dL (−0.47 to 0.98), I² high; one cohort 5.7 → 8.4 mg/dL at week 6; a VLCKD trial −1.23 mg/dL
interactions.population: 10 RCTs; women with PCOS; postmenopausal women with obesity
interactions.mechanism: Ketones compete with urate for renal tubular secretion (rise in weeks 1–6); weight loss lowers it later

interactions.effectSize: Weight-loss diet with 40 % carbohydrate, 30 % protein, 30 % fat: 0.57 → 0.47 mmol/L (≈ 9.6 → 7.9 mg/dL) over 16 weeks
interactions.mechanism: Weight loss and better insulin sensitivity increase renal urate excretion; no sustained ketosis

interactions.effectSize: Total protein not linked to gout; meat RR +41 %, seafood +51 %, dairy −44 % (top vs bottom quintile)
interactions.mechanism: Purine load from meat and fish raises urate; dairy proteins are uricosuric

interactions.effectSize: No data opened; no sustained ketosis expected in a 16 h window
interactions.mechanism: Overnight ketones stay low (< 0.5 mmol/L)

interactions.effectSize: Not measured in sources opened; small transient rise expected
interactions.mechanism: Early ketosis begins competing for tubular secretion

interactions.effectSize: Not measured in sources opened; rise expected as ketones climb (engine: +0.6 mg/dL per mmol/L BHB, proposed)
interactions.mechanism: Ketone–urate competition; rise scales with ketonaemia

interactions.effectSize: 338 → 495 µmol/L (≈ 5.7 → 8.3 mg/dL, +46 %) over 4–21 days; larger rise with higher ketonuria; 1 gout flare in 1422 (a man already treated for gout)
interactions.mechanism: Ketone–urate competition for renal secretion; some tissue catabolism

interactions.effectSize: No data opened
interactions.mechanism: No known direct pathway

interactions.effectSize: No data opened; eggs are low in purines
interactions.mechanism: No purine load

interactions.effectSize: DASH pattern (high fibre, fruit, vegetables, low-fat dairy) −0.25 mg/dL (−0.4 to −0.1); fibre alone not isolated
interactions.mechanism: Pattern effect; attribution to fibre uncertain

interactions.effectSize: No data opened
interactions.mechanism: No known direct pathway

interactions.effectSize: Gout RR 1.32 at 10–14.9 g/d to 2.53 at ≥ 50 g/d; beer RR 1.49 per daily serving, spirits 1.15, wine 1.04 (NS)
interactions.mechanism: Ethanol speeds ATP breakdown to urate and lactate reduces urate excretion; beer adds guanosine

interactions.effectSize: Caffeine and tea not associated with urate; coffee ≥ 6 cups/d −0.43 mg/dL (cross-sectional); coffee meta-analysis: no significant urate difference, gout RR 0.43
interactions.mechanism: The coffee effect is not from caffeine (possibly chlorogenic acids, insulin sensitivity)

interactions.effectSize: No data found
interactions.mechanism: Creatine is cleared as creatinine, not via purines

interactions.effectSize: Skim-milk protein (80 g) lowered urate ~10 % over 3 h; soy protein raised it ~10 %
interactions.mechanism: Milk proteins increase renal urate excretion

interactions.effectSize: Bariatric surgery: transient urate rise and more flares early; later falls
interactions.mechanism: Ketosis and tissue breakdown early; weight loss later

interactions.effectSize: −7.7 kg over 16 weeks: urate −1.7 mg/dL; flares 2.1 → 0.6 per month
interactions.mechanism: Insulin sensitivity raises renal urate excretion

interactions.effectSize: Fructose: gout RR 1.62 (highest vs lowest intake); sugar-sweetened drinks RR 2.08
interactions.mechanism: Fructose phosphorylation depletes ATP and raises urate production; weight gain lowers excretion

interactions.effectSize: No data opened
interactions.mechanism: Hard sessions break down some ATP; effect expected small and transient

interactions.effectSize: Marathon: transient rise in xanthine oxidoreductase activity and urate, resolved by 24 h; chronic effect not shown in sources opened
interactions.mechanism: ATP breakdown to hypoxanthine during very long efforts; dehydration

interactions.effectSize: Sleep apnoea: gout RR 1.29 (1.11–1.48); CPAP lowered urate (Hedges g −0.49). Plain sleep debt: no data opened
interactions.mechanism: Night-time hypoxia raises purine turnover; generalising to sleep debt is a guess

interactions.effectSize: Weight loss 3–34 kg: urate change −168 to +30 µmol/L; ~75 % of studies showed fewer flares
interactions.mechanism: Better insulin sensitivity increases renal urate excretion

interactions.effectSize: Milk-protein effect as for whey (~10 % acute fall)
interactions.mechanism: Dairy protein is uricosuric

interactions.effectSize: Soy protein (80 g) raised urate ~10 % over 3 h; purine-rich vegetables not linked to gout
interactions.mechanism: Soy contains purines

interactions.effectSize: Not measured; expected rise with ketonaemia
interactions.mechanism: Ketone–urate competition

rules.message: Because your fasting glucose was {value} mg/dL on {date}, please answer the diabetes question again. Fasts over 24 h and very-low-carb wait for your answer.
Because your fasting glucose was {value} mg/dL on {date} (prediabetes range), the plan ranks fibre, weight loss and training higher.
Your glucose test on {date} was taken within 3 days of a long fast. Glucose and insulin read high or low then; retest after 2 weeks of normal eating.
Because your fasting glucose was {value} mg/dL on {date}, retest it with HbA1c about 12 weeks after your plan starts.
Because your HbA1c was {value} % on {date}, please answer the diabetes question again. Fasts over 24 h and very-low-carb wait for your answer.
Because your HbA1c was {value} % on {date} (prediabetes range), the plan ranks fibre, weight loss, unsaturated fats and training higher.
Your report shows low haemoglobin or a haemoglobin variant, so your HbA1c of {value} % on {date} may be off. The plan leans on fasting glucose instead.
HbA1c shows about 3 months of glucose. Retest no sooner than 12 weeks after your plan started; an earlier test shows only part of the change.
Because your HbA1c was {value} % on {date}: if you take diabetes medicine, fasting or very-low-carb can drop your sugar too low. Agree any fast with your doctor first.
Because your HOMA-IR was {value} on {date} (from your glucose and insulin), the plan ranks weight loss, fibre, 16:8 eating and training higher.
Insulin tests differ between labs by 15 % or more. Retest at the same lab after about 12 weeks to compare.

when.unit: days after a fast > 36 h, or same morning as coffee

rules.message: Your insulin test on {date} came soon after a long fast or after coffee, which changes insulin for a while. Retest after 2 weeks of normal eating, water only that morning.
Because your uric acid was {value} mg/dL on {date}, fasts over 24 h and very-low-carb can raise it further for a few weeks. Drink at least 2.5 L a day.
Because your uric acid was {value} mg/dL on {date}, fasts are capped at 72 h unless you choose longer after reading the warning.
Because you have gout and your uric acid was {value} mg/dL on {date}, fasts are capped at 24 h. Ask your doctor before anything longer.
Because your uric acid was {value} mg/dL on {date}, the plan counts alcohol against you, beer most and wine least.
Because your uric acid was {value} mg/dL on {date}, the plan prefers dairy protein (curd, paneer, milk, whey) and limits sugary drinks.
Because your uric acid was {value} mg/dL on {date}: very fast weight loss can raise it for a few weeks before it falls. A moderate pace is gentler.
Because your uric acid was {value} mg/dL on {date}, retest it about 8 weeks after starting very-low-carb or any fast over 72 h.
